name: Alert
summary: A brief, important message that draws attention without interrupting the task.
description: An alert tells people something important about the page or what they just did: a saved change, a failed payment, a maintenance window, a quota about to run out. It sits in the content, tinted by its intent with an icon and a title, and is announced by assistive technology when it appears. It never moves focus and never blocks the page: a message that needs a decision is a dialog, a short transient confirmation is a toast.

anatomy.description: Root: the tinted box, announced as an alert when it appears. Carries the intent.
Glyph of the icon font naming the intent (info, check_circle, warning, error). Hidden from assistive technology; the text carries the meaning.
Column holding the title and the message.
Optional short heading of the message, in the intent color.
The message: what happened and what to do, in one or two sentences.

properties.name: Intent
properties.description: What kind of message it is; sets the tint, the border, the icon and the title color.

options.description: Neutral information worth noticing (a maintenance window, a tip).
Something completed as expected (changes saved, payment received).
Something needs attention before it becomes a problem (quota almost reached, unsaved changes).
Something failed or is blocked, with what to do about it.

properties.name: Title
properties.description: Short heading stating the point of the message (Payment failed). Optional when the message is one sentence.

properties.name: Message
properties.description: What happened and what to do, in plain words.

states.description: The only state: an alert has no interaction of its own.

notes: The icon sits before the content, aligned with the first line of text; title and message stack in the content column.
The alert fills the width of its container and grows with its text; it never floats over the content.

name.text: An alert has no accessible name requirement: its content is announced as a whole when it appears. The title and the message are that content; the icon is hidden.

guidelines.text: An alert displays a brief, important message in a way that attracts attention without interrupting the task; it never receives or moves focus, so the person's place in the page is kept.

An alert is a status message: assistive technology announces it when it appears without focus moving to it. Insert the alert in the page when the event happens; content that is already there at page load is not announced.

Render a div with role="alert", an assertive and atomic live region, and insert it (or set its content) at the moment of the event; do not render it empty and fill it later unnoticed, and do not use it for content present at page load.
Mark alert-like components with the liveRegion semantics so accessibility services announce them; use the assertive mode sparingly.
The intent is never conveyed by color alone: the icon and, above all, the title and the message say what kind of message it is (Payment failed), so an alert without its tint still reads.
The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden="true"; an icon-font glyph is written as its ligature name, which would otherwise be read before the message.
Title and message are text in the reading order; the title is the first thing announced, so it states the point.

Title and message text contrast at least 4.5:1 with the alert fill in every color mode and intent: the title 6.92:1 (info), 7.18:1 (success), 7.28:1 (warning) and 5.45:1 (error) in light mode, 11.41:1 or more in dark mode; the message 17.59:1 or more (light) and 9.51:1 or more (dark). The icon contrasts at least 3:1 with the fill: 5.45:1 or more (light), 8.28:1 or more (dark).
The border is decoration: the text identifies the alert, so it needs no 3:1 contrast (the warning border is 2.13:1 in light mode).
An alert that reports an error of a form names the fields in error and what to do; the fields themselves also carry their error.

references.title: APG: Alert pattern, roles, states and properties
MDN: ARIA alert role (assertive live region, dynamic content only)
WCAG technique ARIA19: role=alert or live regions to identify errors
Jetpack Compose accessibility: alerts and pop-ups (liveRegion semantics)

guidelines: The title states the point in a few words: Payment failed, Changes saved, Scheduled maintenance.
The message says what happened and what to do, in one or two plain sentences; with the error intent, how to recover.
Sentence case; the message ends with a period, the title does not.
Say the status in words, never through the color: Your card was declined, not Something went wrong.

props.title: Scheduled maintenance
props.message: The service will be unavailable on Sunday from 02:00 to 04:00 UTC.

props.title: Storage almost full
props.message: You have used 95% of your storage. Delete files or upgrade your plan to keep uploading.

props.title: Payment failed
props.message: Your card was declined. Check the card details or try another payment method.
You can change the language of the interface in Settings.

decisions.text: An alert has four intents, info (default), success, warning and error, each reading the Figma library's functional family: subtle fill global.bg.subtle.functional.<family>.default, border global.border.accent.functional.<family>.default, icon global.icon.on-subtle.functional.<family>.default, title global.text.on-subtle.functional.<family>.default; the message stays in the primary text color.
Each intent has a fixed icon of the icon font: info, check_circle, warning, error, drawn at 24 px before the text; it cannot be changed or removed.
The box has 16 px of padding, 12 px between the icon and the text, 4 px between title and message, a 0.6 px border and 8 px corners; the title is 16 px medium, the message 16 px regular.
The alert has no close button and no actions in this version: dismissing needs script, and actions in a live region are read before people can reach them. Both are open questions.

changelog.note: Initial draft (decisions intents, intent-icons, box, no-dismiss-no-actions). A div with role alert, an intent icon, a title and a message; intents info, success, warning, error; no interaction state. Contrast on the fill, light / dark: title info 6.92 / 11.41, success 7.18 / 12.31, warning 7.28 / 12.85, error 5.45 / 9.60; message 17.59 or more / 9.51 or more; icon 5.45 or more / 8.28 or more; border measured only (warning 2.13 in light mode).
